short: You have read his work for years. You have never once seen his name.

slides.headline: You have read his work for years. You have never once seen his name.

slides.head: Bible Serif. Bible Sans. Bible Slab.
slides.text: Three typefaces Klaus E. Krogh designed for one problem: fitting about 780,000 words onto paper thin enough to carry.

slides.quote: When people see a Bible that they recognize as readable, it's all these choices that made it readable: the typeface, the size, the kerning.

slides.head: Then a stranger asked him for a Bible people with dyslexia could read.
slides.text: The result was Grace, built with researchers at Cambridge University. The letters carry extra weight at the bottom, so b and d stop collapsing into each other.

slides.head: He gave it away.
slides.text: His firm normally sold each typeface to a single publisher. Grace he made free to individuals for personal use. Klaus E. Krogh died on 6 October, aged 74.
